source_review.notes: Checked all six official/primary sources. Current gRPC retry guidance supports transparent versus configured retries, commitment after response headers, per-method attempt/status/backoff, jitter, throttling, pushback, and attempt observability. AWS Builders' Library and Architecture Blog support timeout-aware capped backoff, jitter variants, token budgets, and synchronized-load reasoning. Google SRE supports randomized exponential backoff, one-layer ownership, per-request/fleet retry budgets, 4^3 amplification, overload positive feedback, and server/client control. RFC 9110 supports Retry-After semantics. Product-specific mechanisms are not generalized beyond their scopes.

evidence: Checked total attempts A, retry index k, base b, multiplier g, cap c, jitter J_k, probability p, layers L/A_l, initial/retry rates lambda_0/lambda_r, and ratio rho for consistent domains.
Confirmed full jitter interval and expectation, truncated geometric sum, and nested product distinguish average from correlated worst case.
Confirmed maximum attempts includes initial and retry indices count A-1 delays.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Logical-operation identity remains separate from each transport attempt.

evidence: Recomputed bounds 80,160,320,500 ms and full-jitter expected waits 40+80+160+250=530 ms; worst delays total 1,060 ms.
Recomputed five-attempt 1.4-second feasibility: 1,300 ms after reserve leaves only 240 ms after worst delays, insufficient for four 220 ms retry attempts.
Recomputed nested attempts as 3^3=27 and expected four-attempt truncated geometric at p=0.2 as 1+0.2+0.04+0.008=1.248.
Recomputed 8% of 20,000/s as 1,600 retries/s; counted ten examples and five answer pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Independence/expected-delay values are explanatory, not outage capacity guarantees.

evidence: Constructed deterministic synchronized-client trace and confirmed jitter spreads times but does not reduce count.
Constructed timeout-after-commit trace proving same effect ID/outcome query is required.
Expanded nested attempts to confirm product bound and one-owner reduction.
Confirmed retry admissibility requires class+safety+deadline+budget jointly; no single predicate suffices.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Load bounds hold only over the stated budget scope and visible retry layers.

evidence: Reviewed pre-send, partial send, application receipt, commit-before-response, partial body/batch/stream, redirects/endpoints/regions, process restart, and DLQ/redrive.
Reviewed validation/auth/policy/conflict/domain/expired, 429/503/overload, transparent/library, nested, deadline/cancel, and uncertain effects.
Reviewed RNG clones/rounding/overflow, malformed/huge/date pushback, autoscaling token multiplication, tenant abuse, synchronized failure/recovery, and regional authority.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans correctness, timing, capacity, topology, persistence, and hostile inputs.

evidence: Confirmed every attempt preserves operation/effect ID and fingerprint.
Confirmed one owner, explicit total attempts, original deadline, cancellable capped jitter, and pushback are enforced.
Confirmed retry tokens do not bypass admission/circuit/tenant fairness and overload suppresses attempts.
Confirmed batch/queue/stream retries preserve item/message/position identity, order, age, and terminal path.
invariant_checking.notes: Success-after-retry is never allowed to hide initial-failure health.

evidence: Reviewed idempotent-effect proof and confirmed authoritative same-key protocol/retention is necessary.
Reviewed jitter argument and confirmed it provides desynchronization rather than capacity.
Reviewed token-budget argument and confirmed per-instance scope is insufficient under autoscaling.
Reviewed independent expectation versus correlated outage counterexample.
proof_review.notes: No retry mechanism is claimed to create recovery or exactly-once effects by itself.

evidence: Confirmed proof sketch names identity, budget scope, correlation, semantic safety, and hidden-layer limitations.
Confirmed gRPC/AWS/Google/IETF behavior is attributed and configuration scoped.
Confirmed algorithms, design policy, and empirical obligations remain distinct.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Library transparent retry is an explicit inventory obligation.

evidence: All six official/primary references were retrieved or checked on 2026-09-02 where current guidance applies.
All rates, client counts, probabilities, delays, attempts, and recovery ratios are labeled scenarios.

Actual recovery probability, safe spare capacity, SDK/mesh behavior, token scope, jitter distribution, pushback, idempotency retention, marginal benefit, and outage dynamics remain explicit integration/load/fault evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production client fleet, dependency, provider, or retry configuration was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed operation/attempt identity, classification, safety, capped backoff/jitter, pushback, deadlines, retry ownership, fleet budgets, overload coordination, batch/queue/stream behavior, observability, and verification as one feedback-control model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through method decision tables, same-key outcome query, explicit SDK policies, cancellable jitter, Retry-After validation, remaining-budget checks, retry-token/bulkhead/circuit integration, persisted asynchronous counters, attempt spans, and synchronized fault/load tests.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module develops retries from identity and failure classification through timing and fleet stability, then applies them to overload, batches, queues, streams, and verification. Ten examples and five increasingly integrative exercises have complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
